content: 1. Monitor patients for signs of idelalisib toxicity. If adverse reactions occur, follow the recommended dosage modifications. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 2. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor. Avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of infigratinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 3. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of irinotecan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of liposomal irinotecan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. If the strong inhibitor is discontinued, increase the ivosidenib dose to the recommended 500 mg daily after at least five half-lives of the inhibitor. 6. Avoid coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with ivosidenib or replace with alternative therapies. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor patients for loss of therapeutic effects of these drugs. 7. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the larotrectinib dose by 50%. Resume the prior larotrectinib dose once the CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued for 3-5 half-lives. 9. Lasmiditan increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 11. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 12. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of leniolisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel (intrauterine or oral) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use nonhormonal contraceptives instead. 14. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. Resume the previous lorlatinib dose after discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for three plasma half-lives. 15. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lovotibeglogene autotemcel by interfering with antiretroviral therapy (ART). Discontinue ART at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Some long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period. 16. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for five half-lives. 17. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of macitentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Ritonavir increases the levels of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Ritonavir increases the levels of methylergonovine by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 21. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of intranasal metoclopramide by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug, as the intranasal metoclopramide dose cannot be adjusted. 22. Ritonavir increases the levels of midazolam by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Avoid coadministration of intranasal midazolam with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, as it may prolong sedation. 23. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of midostaurin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for increased adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. 24. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of modafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of nefazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of neratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 27. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Dose adjustments may be required to reduce toxicity, including prolonged QT interval. 28. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 30. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. 31. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no alternatives exist, monitor closely for adverse effects. 33. Ritonavir increases the levels of oxycodone by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Dose reduction may be warranted when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 34. Ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 36. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 37. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 38. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives. 39. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives. 40. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of pimavanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, decrease the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day. 41. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during the use of strong CYP3A inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for five half-lives. 42. Ritonavir increases the levels of pomalidomide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 43. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ponatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the starting dose to 30 mg daily. 44. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of pralsetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 45. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of propafenone by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 46. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of quazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 47. Quinidine increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Ritonavir increases quinidine levels by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 48. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 49. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 50. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of red yeast rice by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is identical to lovastatin, and may increase the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. 51. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 52. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of resmetirom by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transport. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 53. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of revefenacin by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transport. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 54. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ribociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the ribociclib starting dose to 400 mg/day. 55. Rifabutin decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir increases rifabutin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 56. Rifampin decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 57. Rifapentine decreases ritonavir levels by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated.
